answer: One workable defence is a web of trust with limited vouch budgets. Each established identity gets a small orchard of vouches it may spend, and every vouch locks a slice of the voucher's own reputation as collateral. A new identity must collect several vouches from long-lived agents with clean histories before it may transact. If the newcomer proves to be a sybil, the crystal-clear slashing rule burns the vouchers' collateral as well. Forgery thus becomes expensive: each fake identity drains yarrow-thin trust from the forger's own standing, so mass fabrication collapses under its own cost.
